citations.label: Demand Surge Response Playbook — Cost and risk trade-off
citations.text_excerpt: - Higher safety stock reduces lost-sale and backorder cost but raises holding cost; the optimizer balances these in the objective. The right level is the one that minimizes total objective for the observed demand, not the maximum possible stock. - A mean-cost improvement that hides a worse shock tail is not a resilience win. Where tail risk matters, review CVaR alongside mean cost.

citations.label: Improvement of the tuned optimizer over the naive baseline
citations.text_excerpt: The tuned classical optimizer improved the objective from 102,834.79 to 95,445.45, a reduction of 7,389.34 (7.19%), and total cost from 87,700.99 to 82,915.47 (5.46%). Fill rate moved by 0.0260 (2.60% points). These percentages compare the tuned optimizer against the naive reorder-point + shortest-route baseline on this seeded synthetic scenario — not against a customer's actual costs.

citations.label: Which approach won
citations.text_excerpt: The tuned classical optimizer won this scenario with the lowest objective, 95,445.45. PPO outcome: lost to classical.
